old_problem: Although UCE severity is established by title/Criteria/errortype1, the command's errorlocation selectors conflict between Socket and IOD/CCD meanings, so neither direction nor expected destructive disposition is authoritative.
disposition_reason: The copied Correctable labels can be rejected, but that does not resolve the proprietary endpoint selector. For xGMI UCE, choosing the wrong peer/direction or expected sync-flood/reset behavior changes both coverage and recovery. ED-16 requires exact vendor semantics and a separately authorized recovery before injection. No standard source can safely infer this AMD tool field, so Pending/BLOCKED is retained.
decision_basis: Read Reliability row 41, AI fields, historical record 2444 and next pending row 42.
Preserved UCE because title, Criteria and errortype1 agree, while explicitly rejecting copied Correctable step labels.
Did not infer Socket1/0 from errorlocation0/1 given adjacent IOD/CCD usage.
Kept each direction as an independent hazardous checkpoint with two-peer evidence.
No injector, reset, power or DUT activity occurred.

test_case.test_name: xGMI3 uncorrectable event by peer direction
test_case.purpose: Validate the approved uncorrectable xGMI response for each required peer direction with attributable source/destination evidence, predicted containment and recovered coherent fabric.
required_package: Authoritative multi-socket xGMI topology and direction map
AMD tool/spec hash/license defining errorlocation selectors
errortype1 UCE and per-direction containment/reset semantics
Linux/Windows, peer counters, OOB and management oracle
One-shot authorization, abort, recovery and BIOS/HDT restoration
test_case.test_command: Do not execute the placeholder commands. After the AMD owner maps errorlocation to exact endpoint/direction, authorize one UCE only, capture continuous OOB plus both peers' tool/OS/counter evidence, perform the signed recovery, restore the platform, and require a new authorization before another direction.
test_case.expected_result: The selected direction produces the exact approved UCE and containment within deadline, both sockets and the coherent link recover to baseline, and later separately authorized directions meet the same attributable requirements.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS is available until selector and containment semantics are authoritative. Tool PASS, assumed Socket labels, a copied Correctable event, an uncontrolled crash or a chained peer injection cannot pass.
safety_gate: Dedicated non-production multi-socket SUT with OOB power/reimage recovery.
One direction only after selector, severity and expected disposition are signed.
Abort on wrong endpoint, storm, unexpected reset, peer isolation, degraded link or lost console.
Never automatically retry or authorize the next direction.
expected_evidence: Package provenance and exact one-direction command
Continuous OOB plus source/peer UCE evidence
Expected containment and bounded recovery timeline
Fabric integrity, full restoration and verdict
test_case.recovery: Currently depends on unresolved containment semantics. The platform/AMD owner must define reset, power or reimage recovery for each expected disposition and prove both peers return healthy before execution can be unblocked.
